title: Vertically opposite angles, straight lines and angles at a point
summary: Apply the three core angle facts at intersections and around a point.
objectives: Apply vertically opposite, straight-line and angles-at-a-point facts.
Form equations from angle expressions at intersections.
Check that calculated angles satisfy the relevant 180° or 360° total.

blocks.text: Vertically opposite angles are equal, adjacent angles on a straight line total 180°, and angles around a point total 360°.

At an intersection, vertically opposite angles are the non-adjacent pair across the vertex and are equal. Adjacent angles on a straight line total 180°. All angles around the point total 360°. Mark one known angle first, then propagate only relationships that share the same vertex.

When algebraic expressions label vertically opposite angles, equate them. When expressions label an adjacent linear pair, add them and set the sum to 180°. A reliable check is to alternate the two angle sizes around a two-line intersection and verify that all four total 360°.

sections.title: Worked example

prompt.text: Two intersecting lines make an obtuse angle of 124°. Find either acute angle.

sections.verification_note: The result follows the stated property and satisfies the original geometric conditions.

prompt.text: Vertically opposite angles are (5x+7)° and (8x−38)°. Find every angle at the intersection.

content.text: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so 5x+7=8x−38.
Solve 45=3x to obtain x=15. Each of that opposite pair is 82°.
Each adjacent angle is 180°−82°=98°, so the four angles alternate 82°, 98°, 82°, 98°.

blocks.text: Do not equate adjacent angles unless another fact says they are equal. A straight line gives a total of 180°, while angles around a point give 360°. State the angle fact before writing the equation so the correct total is clear.

prompt.text: One angle on a straight line is 73°. Find the other.

feedback.text: Angles on a straight line total 180°, so 180 - 73 = 107.
